title: The Block City Night Wave
premise: A caretaker wants to dim a toy city at bedtime, but the control is on a roof across the map. A prearranged sequence of mechanical shutters closes one window and exposes a reflector to the next, carrying a visible dimming wave across the city while leaving a moonlit path home.
hook: Bedtime is crossing town one window at a time.
visible_action: Shutters descend; tiny reflectors rotate; the next latch releases; lighted windows fade along a serpentine route; a path remains lit.
intended_takeaway_or_theme: A sequence can carry a signal while preserving one needed exception.
gate: Use an internally defined optical-mechanical toy rule; not real electrical or building-safety guidance.

style_application.material: Original block materials with soft practical light
style_application.why: Visible polygon facets and a coordinated wave make scale and sequence readable.
style_application.check: Check geometry, consistent lights, nonflashing timing and the propagation rule.

editorial_pick.original_reason: A city-wide night wave offers a satisfying visual payoff and reusable timing controls.
editorial_pick.proposed_first_version: A miniature block city passes one intentional evening signal from place to place. Let the camera reveal the larger pattern slowly.
editorial_pick.gate: Check the actual causal or fictional rule and avoid flashing lights or excessive brightness changes.
editorial_pick.note: These are the catalogue's historical editorial recommendations, not current owner-approved selections or guaranteed watchable stories. Reapply the latest comedy/suspense gate.
